A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LiMoE. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, cross-dataset transfer, corruption robustness, and ablation results, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original empirical results and adds object detection experiments and controls for representation diversity and mixing strategies.

M1.justification: Section 7.3 adds a detection adaptation that distills the three representation experts into VoxelNet during CML and uses CenterPoint for downstream fine-tuning. The original CML/SMS components, losses, and pseudocode remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v2 adds 3D object detection on nuScenes, extending evaluation beyond semantic segmentation to a distinct prediction task. The existing eleven-dataset coverage, including corruption scenarios, is retained.

E2.justification: The existing segmentation comparator sets remain. New comparisons introduce GCC-3D in the detection table and three-MinkUNet, concatenation, addition, and averaging controls in Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: The added detection evaluation uses CenterPoint, 5%, 10%, and 20% training-data proportions, and mAP/NDS metrics. The new ablations introduce homogeneous-expert and alternative-fusion controls. These are additional evaluation designs; the original segmentation protocols and training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Tables 7–8 add two substantive tests of the central design: heterogeneous representations versus three identical voxel experts, and learned MoE mixing versus concatenation, addition, and averaging. The earlier expert-combination, backbone, robustness, and qualitative analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experiments continue the existing practice of reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds detection and control results while retaining the earlier segmentation and robustness scores. At 5% detection training data, SuperFlow+LiMoE reports 47.3 mAP/55.3 NDS versus SuperFlow's 46.0/54.9. Table 8 shows averaging ties LiMoE in three of five settings. SMS's 85.8M parameters and 8.3 FPS are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The representation definitions, CML/SMS equations, and evaluation formulas are mathematically unchanged. No new assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the three-stage framework, claimed novelty of MoE for LiDAR representation learning, and effectiveness across eleven datasets. The added experiments support these claims without redefining the main contributions.

C2.justification: New discussion attributes gains to representation diversity beyond identical-expert ensembles and to adaptive feature selection over simple mixing. The efficiency paragraph now characterizes SMS as efficient at 8.3 FPS. Existing qualifications about unavailable sensor FoV information and SMS computational costs remain.

D1.justification: v2 specifies VoxelNet/CenterPoint for the detection extension and discloses SMS's parameter count and throughput, although the throughput measurement conditions remain unspecified. Existing training hyperparameters, pseudocode, and resource links are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for GCC-3D, SECOND, CenterPoint, and Nair and Hinton's activation-function work. The related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain essentially unchanged; publication updates to existing references do not represent new cited works.

P1.justification: v2 replaces the main-text backbone discussion with the representation-diversity ablation, adds acknowledgments and appendix subsections, and makes small wording edits. The backbone study remains in the appendix, and most existing prose and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact experimental tables, relocates Table 4, and renumbers the original per-class Tables 6–7 as Tables 9–10. Existing figures and algorithm displays are largely retained, with page and column reflow.

improvement.justification: The detection evaluation and diversity/fusion controls strengthen the empirical support beyond v1's existing segmentation study, while parameter and throughput reporting improve cost transparency. The gain is bounded: averaging ties LiMoE in three Table 8 settings, uncertainty remains unreported, and the new efficiency characterization lacks measurement context. Overall, v2 provides useful additional validation without substantially revising the core contribution.
